AKM Faiz with Parvin Hannan, Advocates— For the Petitioner. 
Md Abdur Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State. 
AJ Mohammad Ali, Advocate—For added Opposite Party No. 3.
parties:
Monowar Islam alias Monu ------ Petitioner
Vs
State and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Awlad Ali J: This Rule at the instance of the petitioner upon an application under section 561A Cr PC was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner Sylhet and District Anti-Corruption Officer, Sylhet to show cause as to why the Inquiry Proceeding being No. Sylhet DAB E/R No. 06/97 should not be quashed. Material facts necessary for the appreciation of law involved in this case are that, the petitioner being the plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet on 24-11-96 alleging that he went to the Tahsil Office for payment of rent and he came to know that the suit land has been recorded in the name of Sree Probir Kumar Chakroborty although the same ought to have been recorded in the name of the plaintiff and/or their predecessor Abdur Rouf. In the suit the Court issued summons upon the defendants on 27-1-97. The plaintiff also made a prayer for keeping some documents in the safe custody of the Court which was allowed on 27-1-97. It has been stated by the petitioner that a petition of complaint was lodged before the Magistrate, Sadar, Sylhet by one Isab Ali on 9-12-96 against the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 132/96 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet alleging, inter alia, that the petitioner and others committed forgery and submitted a false pattanama in the said suit which is pending and prayed for taking necessary action under sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 of the Penal Code. The petition of complaint was sent to the District Anti Corruption Bureau for taking appropriate action and District Anti-Corruption Bureau started a proceedings against the present petitioner and others vide Memo No. 106/DAB dated 16-1-97. A prayer was made by the District Anti Corruption Officer before the Subordinate Judge for seizing the pattanama and the learned Subordinate Judge directed the anti-corruption officer for seeking permission from the learned District Judge. The District Anti-corruption Inspector made a prayer before the District Judge for seizing the document in question and the learned District Judge allowed the prayer and by his Memo No. 74 dated 2-2-97 informed the District Anti-Corruption Bureau that the prayer for seizing the document namely, the pattanama dated 14 4 44 lying before the Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 132 of 1996, has been allowed pursuant to the above memo issued by the learned District Judge. The learned Subordinate Judge 2nd Court Sylhet by his order dated 1-3-97 gave permission to Mr Md Jasimuddin Gazi Assistant Inspector, Bureau of District Anti-Corruption Sylhet to seize the patta dated 14-4-44, and further ordered to hand over the said document to the Assistant Inspector from the safe custody of the court. On 5-3-97 the learned Subordinate Judge as per order dated 2-2-97 directed the Shrestadar to hand over the said document to Mr Md Jasimuddin, Assistant Inspector, DAB, Sylhet after preparing the seizure list. 

 2. That one Isab Ali made an application before this Court praying for being added as opposite party in the present Rule and he was made opposite party No. 3. In the application for addition of party he has stated that a petition of complaint has been filed before the Magistrate, 1st Class by the opposite party No. 3 for taking action against Monowar Islam and others under sections 420, 467, 468, 472, 34 of the Penal Code and the petition of complaint was registered as Application No. 126 of 1996 and the learned Magistrate sent the petition of complaint to the District Anti Corruption Bureau, Sylhet and directed for an enquiry and report. In the petition of complaint it has been alleged that accused No. 1 Monowar Islam @ Manu filed Title Suit No. 132 of 1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet impleading Indian Nationals as defendants showing their residence at Sylhet. In the suit a forged patta and some other papers have been filed. The plaintiff has retained the original copy of the forged patta and submitted a photostat copy. It has also been stated in the petition of complaint that regarding the self same land the petitioner had filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1981 in the Court of Additional Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet and obtained a decree against the predecessor of the accused Nos. 1-4 and the said decree was upheld up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. The accused in collusion with each other and in order to deprive the complainant of the decree as aforesaid filed the present Title Suit by forging papers and documents impleading the Indian nationals as defendants. The opposite party No. 3 has stated that in the facts and circumstances the complaint was filed for the purpose of making investigation into the allegation of forgery of a patta dated 14-4-44 and to prosecute the accused in accordance with law. 

 3. Mr AKM Faiz, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, contends that the order of the learned District Judge according permission to the Anti-Corruption Bureau for seizing the documents namely, pattanama, from the civil Court is illegal and without jurisdiction. He further contends that the proceeding before the District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Sylhet is illegal and consequently, the investigation proceeding before the District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Sylhet is liable to be struck down and or quashed. His submission is that in the facts of the case the learned District Judge had no legal authority to accord permission to seize the document from the civil Court records in respect of which the suit is pending and the document is also under the custody of the Court, and if the inquiry proceeding initiated by the District Anti-Corruption Bureau on the permission given by the District Judge is allowed to proceed, that will be an abuse of the process of the Court. On this proposition Mr Faiz sought reliance from a decision in the case of SM Hafizuddin Ahmed vs Jamaluddin Ahmed, Sub Inspector of Police and others reported in 37 DLR 207. In the case under reference the fact was that a suit was instituted for specific performance of contract on the basis of written agreement for sale dated 7-1-1981 and the suit was decreed ex parte by judgment and order dated 29-6-83. The suit having been decreed the petitioner was allowed to take back his document from the court. The plaintiff as decree holder put the decree in execution on 28-8-83 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The executing Court executed and registered a deed of conveyance in favour of the plaintiff on 6-12-83 in the office of the District Registrar, Dhaka in terms of the decree. The plaintiff then filed an application for issuance of writ of delivery of possession of the decretal property. While the matter was pending for giving delivery of possession an application dated 6-6-84 was addressed to the Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka by one Jamaluddin Ahmed, Sub-inspector of Police, CID Bangladesh. It was stated in that application that the Sub Inspector was asked by the Police Head Quarter to enquire into the forged Bainanama submitted by the plaintiff petitioner in the revision Case as opposite party No. 4 Jane Alam had submitted a prayer that the said bainama was a forged one and the decree in the aforesaid suit was passed on the basis of the forged bainanama. Then the Sub-Inspector prayed for permission to conduct an enquiry in the matter and to take the bainanama in the custody for comparison and opinion. The Subordinate Judge on perusal of the application observed in his order dated 9-6-84 that necessary permission was required to be obtained from the District Judge. His order dated 20-6-84 showed that another application was filed by the Sub-Inspector to the District Judge which was forwarded to him with an order of the District Judge for according permission. Accordingly, permission was accorded for seizure of the document in question. On the following day the Subordinate Judge passed order for refiling the Bainanama and further observed that the police officer concerned may seize the document direct from the plaintiff or he might wait till the document was refiled in Court. It was contended that the civil Court illegally divested itself of its jurisdiction to hold an enquiry into the alleged forgery in the disputed Bainapatra and further illegally permitted the Criminal Investigation Department police to usurp the function of the Court vested in it under section 476 of the Cr PC and on such contention it was held that although it is true to say that a proceeding for quashment is considered premature at the stage of inquiry or investigation but in the facts of the present case we think that according of permission by the District Judge to the police amounts to an abuse of the process of the Court. It was further observed that the law requires that the Court itself to hold an inquiry, if necessary, in a matter like this and the Court cannot divest itself of its jurisdiction to hold such inquiry and allow another agency to conduct the same. This, in our opinion, being the position in law, we think that both the District Judge and the Subordinate Judge acted illegally in permitting the Criminal Investigation Department, Sub-Inspector to seize the disputed document and to hold inquiry. In the instant case the admitted fact is that, the document is still lying in the custody of the Court in a proceeding of civil suit and the claim of the present petitioner is based on the pattanama in question although it has not been used or given in evidence and in such circumstances whether any criminal investigating agency shall have the access to the civil Court''s record to seize the document for the purpose of investigation on the allegation of forgery. 

 It would appear from the aforesaid provision that if any Court or any officer in charge of a police station considers that the production of the document or other thing is necessary for the purpose of any investigation, inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code by or before such Court or officer such Court may issue a summons or such officer a written order to the person in whose possession or power such document is believed to be, requiring him to attend and produce it or to produce it at the time and place stated in the summons or order. In this case neither the learned Magistrate in whose Court the petition of complaint was lodged nor any police officer issued any summons or written order requiring the petitioner to produce the document in question, namely, the pattanama. It is enjoined by law that when the proceeding is pending before the Magistrate no notice can be issued by the police. So, in such circumstances permission was sought to be obtained from the learned District Judge to have access to the civil Court record and for seizing the document in question. It has been noticed by us that no summons was issued to the petitioner by the Magistrate in whose Court the complaint was pending as per sub-section (1) of section 94 of the Code. Admittedly, the criminal proceeding on the allegation of forgery is pending before the Magistrate and the alleged forged document is lying in the record pending civil suit. In the proviso to section 94 Cr PC the power of the Sessions Judge to accord permission is clearly enumerated. The proviso says no such officer as contemplated under sub-section (1) of section 94 shall issue any order requiring the production of any document which is in the custody of a Bank or banker as defined in the Bankers'' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and which relates to the bank account of any person. But for the purpose of investigation an offence under sections 403, 406, 408 and 409 and sections 421 to 424 (both inclusive) and section 465 to section 477A (both inclusive) of the Penal Code relating to any document as envisaged in the proviso aforesaid such officer can issue order for production of document with the prior permission in writing of a Sessions Judge. It is not clearly enjoined by law as laid down that the Sessions Judge has unrestricted power to give authority to any investigating agency like police officer, Anti-corruption Inspector to seize the document from the custody of a competent civil Court in connection with a civil suit. More so when the criminal proceeding is pending before the Magistrate on the basis of a complaint. 

 6. What has been laid down by their Lordships in 37 DLR as discussed above can apply to the extent that the Sessions Judge had no power to accord permission when admittedly the patta in question has been produced before the Civil Court in connection with a Civil Proceeding initiated by the petitioner as in that case the civil Court will divest itself of its jurisdiction to hold any enquiry as to the allegation of forgery. Although the plaintiff has not used the document in the civil Court and nor the document has been given in evidence but the fact remains that the suit is pending and the document has been filed in the suit which is under the custody of the Court and the added opposite party has already appeared before the civil Court and filed an application for being added as defendant in the suit. And during hearing we are also informed by Mr AKM Faiz that the added opposite party who is a complainant in the criminal case has been impleaded as defendant in the suit. In such circumstances this added opposite party being the defendant in the suit can very well resist the claim of the plaintiff in respect of the property for which he had already obtained a decree and that has been Upheld by the superior Court and can also pursue the Civil Court to have the alleged patta inquired into the proceeding of the suit in order to determine the genuineness of the patta in question. If the civil Court after making proper inquiry at the proceeding of the suit finds that the document is a forged document a criminal case can be initiated by the Court concerned in accordance with provision of section 476 Cr PC. But before making any such inquiry by the civil Court the Criminal investigating agency on the permission given by the Sessions Judge cannot seize the document for the purpose of investigation. Because in that case the Court will divest itself of its jurisdiction to hold any such inquiry on the allegation of the document being forged. 

 8. In view of the facts and circumstances it is our considered opinion that the District Judge has not exercised his power in the matter of granting permission to the Anti-corruption Inspector to seize the document in question in accordance with law and consequently, the inquiry proceeding vide No Sylhet DAB, E/R No. 06/97 by the District Anti-Corruption Officer is without jurisdiction and the same is liable to be struck down and/or quashed. But, in any event the added opposite party being the defendant in the pending suit will have the chance to make his claim in respect of the property and also to have the patta in question inquired into by the civil Court for determining the allegation of forgery and his interest will be better protected in the civil Court. It is noted that the patta in question should be kept in the custody of the Court till the trial of the suit is concluded.
